candidates.name: city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration
candidates.what_it_holds: Git-scraping pipeline that downloads Toronto's official 'Short Term Rentals Registration' Open Data dataset (short-term-rental-registrations-data.csv) daily at UTC midnight and commits each day's snapshot to git history; 917 commits at time of check, so the commit log is itself a de facto daily point-in-time vintage series of Toronto STR registration counts/addresses going back to whenever the repo started.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a genuine day-by-day point-in-time STR registration panel for a major North American market (Toronto) via git-log archaeology — directly answers gap #4 (point-in-time vintages) and gap #12 (city STR registration datasets, Toronto named explicitly) even though Toronto isn't in our existing 25-dataset municipal STR list.
candidates.time_coverage: daily snapshots, git history depth unknown but 917 commits imply well over 2 years if daily
candidates.size_hint: single CSV re-committed daily; row count not confirmed
candidates.license: repo has a LICENSE file; type not confirmed from fetch
candidates.last_activity: active as of check (git-scraping cron still running per commit count)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: we hold Austin, Barcelona HUTB, Maui, NYC OSE, CA TOT (482 cities) — Toronto not currently in our municipal STR list

candidates.name: TOHS-tool-rbc (Rental Background Check)
candidates.what_it_holds: Daily GitHub-Actions pipeline normalizing Toronto Short-Term Rental Registry data plus Ontario Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) order catalogue, Toronto RentSafeTO, active building permits, multi-tenant house licences and planned developments into address-keyed JSON files (data/a.json ... data/z.json, data/0-9.json); 392 commits, code MIT-licensed, published data dual-licensed under Open Government Licence Toronto/Ontario.
candidates.why_useful: Broader than the Toronto STR-only mirror above — bundles STR registration with landlord/tenant enforcement and building-permit data for the same city, useful for cross-referencing registration compliance with housing-supply signals; also a working template for building a similar address-keyed daily STR+housing pipeline for a US city.
candidates.size_hint: 27 partitioned JSON files, address-keyed, size unconfirmed
candidates.license: code MIT; data under Open Government Licence – Toronto / Ontario
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: partially overlaps candidate above for the STR slice; adds LTB/permits not in our holdings

candidates.name: robbins
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit app + DuckDB/dbt warehouse for Seattle-metro public data; explicitly ingests Seattle's Short-Term Rental License dataset (Socrata id s7df-xba4, ~8,100 records per the city portal) alongside other Socrata SODA API, ArcGIS FeatureServer and federal-bulk-file sources; author states the pipeline is 'replicable across cities through configuration changes only'.
candidates.why_useful: A working, documented one-command pull for Seattle STR licenses (one of the named theme cities) plus a config-driven pattern that could be repointed at Denver/Nashville/Chicago/SF Socrata STR endpoints with minimal work — directly useful as acquisition-method tooling for gap #12 and #17 (Socrata discovery/client tooling).
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot via live Socrata pull, not a historical archive
candidates.size_hint: ~8,100 Seattle STR license records (per city portal, not committed to repo)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Seattle not in our current 25-dataset municipal STR list

candidates.name: strr (UPGo McGill)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package from an academic urban-planning lab (McGill) for cleaning and analysing raw AirDNA-format STR data: functions to compress/expand property-level and daily-level AirDNA tables, flag commercial multi-listing operators, detect 'ghost hostels', and match listings to housing units; 422 commits, 5 stars, includes a data-raw folder. No specific cities/countries fixed in the docs — designed to work on whatever AirDNA extract is supplied.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from AirDNA-style sources) — an academically vetted, reusable toolkit for processing any AirDNA sample export we might obtain, including commercial-operator and ghost-hostel classification that could feed a supply/professionalization signal.
candidates.geography: not city-specific (built for AirDNA-format data generally; UPGo's own work covers Canadian cities)
candidates.size_hint: R package, not a dataset itself
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: no direct duplicate; complements our note that AirDNA-style exports are a HIGH-value gap

candidates.name: NOLA-STR
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed New Orleans short-term-rental license data as of March 2018, paired with 2016 ACS Census demographic data, R parsing scripts and an interactive Leaflet map (index.html/map.html/site.html) of STR license distribution by neighborhood; 19 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A committed historical (2018) snapshot of New Orleans STR licenses that predates our current New Orleans regulatory holdings — useful as an older vintage point for a longer STR-supply time series in that market, and the mapping code is reusable.
candidates.size_hint: small; one static license file plus Census join
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: New Orleans is in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel and referenced in municipal STR list context; this is an older, license-based (not listing-based) cut

candidates.name: short-term-rentals-dash-app
candidates.what_it_holds: Plotly Dash app that pulls New Orleans short-term-rental permit applications live from data.nola.gov's Socrata API (app-token authenticated) rather than committing CSVs; includes a Jupyter notebook documenting the cleaning steps and the column-name differences between the API and CSV download paths; 14 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A small but concrete worked example of pulling New Orleans STR permit-application data (distinct from license data) via Socrata API with documented cleaning quirks — minor value as a method reference, not as a dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: live pull, no historical archive committed
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: New Orleans STR method already partly covered by our Socrata familiarity; adds permit-application angle vs license angle

candidates.name: short-term-rental-spec
candidates.what_it_holds: Official City of Los Angeles GitHub org repo containing the Platform Sharing API specification (platform-sharing/v1.0.yaml, also on SwaggerHub) that STR platforms use to report listing compliance data to LA under the Home-Sharing Ordinance; Apache-2.0 licensed, 39 commits, actively maintained by the city itself.
candidates.why_useful: Not a dataset, but the authoritative schema for what compliance/registration fields LA (and any city adopting the same open spec) actually captures on STR platforms — useful for understanding what a scraped or FOIA'd LA HSO extract would contain, and it is a government-maintained repo (credible, low-risk source) rather than a third party's guess.
candidates.geography: Los Angeles, CA (spec has been referenced/adopted by other cities)
candidates.last_activity: 39 commits, described as under active development
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: LA HSO is a named theme city but not confirmed already in our 25-dataset municipal STR list

candidates.name: sodapy-tutorial-nyc-opendata
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed, three-notebook tutorial (API basics, SoQL query language, sample 311-data analysis) for pulling any Socrata-backed open-data portal via the sodapy Python client; 45 commits; not STR-specific but the exact mechanism needed for Nashville, Seattle, Denver, Chicago, Boston (Analyze Boston) and San Diego open-data portals, all of which run Socrata.
candidates.why_useful: Directly serves gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery clients to find STR datasets across cities) — a clean, documented starting point for writing one reusable puller against the Socrata SODA API that could hit Nashville/Seattle/Denver/Chicago/Boston/San Diego STR endpoints identified in this same search.
candidates.geography: generic (NYC used as the worked example)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: no direct duplicate; complements Socrata-sourced STR datasets already in our municipal list

candidates.name: ltr_license_scraper_portland
candidates.what_it_holds: Python 3.11+ scraper (requests + pandas) that downloads Portland, MAINE's Long-Term Rental (not short-term) landlord license list since Jan 1 2022 from the city website, saving a CSV with a JSON detail column per license; GPL-3.0, archived/read-only as of 13 Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Wrong city (Portland, Maine, not Portland, Oregon) and wrong rental type (LTR landlord licensing, not STR) — flagged only as a reusable scraper template for building an equivalent one against Portland, Oregon's ASTR permit registry or another city's licence portal that lacks a Socrata API.
candidates.geography: Portland, Maine (template transferable to Portland, OR or other non-Socrata city license sites)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: no overlap; not STR, not one of the target cities

notes: This session's shared WebSearch budget (200 calls, pooled across all concurrent scout agents) was exhausted mid-run after 16 queries, before Chicago-specific, San Diego-specific, and Honolulu-specific GitHub repos beyond generic search snippets could be more thoroughly chased, and before an 'awesome-opendata' / Kaggle / Zenodo pass could run at all — a follow-up scout with a fresh budget should target: (a) Chicago BACP STR operator-license dataset specifically (data.cityofchicago.org, likely Socrata) via a mirror/scraper repo, (b) San Diego STRO licenses (data.sandiego.gov, ArcGIS-backed, ~7,954 active licenses per tier — no GitHub mirror found yet), (c) Honolulu DPP STR registration (small, ~1,800 active registrations vs ~7,900 Oahu listings — no GitHub repo found; likely nothing exists given the small program size), (d) HSOConnect/HSO-Connect (github.com/HSOConnect/HSO-Connect) surfaced once as an LA-adjacent 'Data and Modeling Resource Portal' companion repo but could not be verified as holding real data before the budget ran out. Most municipalities (Austin, Denver, Boston, Nashville) publish STR data directly on Socrata/ArcGIS portals with no GitHub mirror at all — the highest-value GitHub finds are the Canadian city daily git-scrape pipelines (Toronto), which are not currently in our municipal STR holdings list despite Toronto being named in gap #12, and the AirDNA-processing tooling (UPGo-McGill/strr) which is method not data. Recommend a teammate try `gh search` (blocked for this web-modality scout by instruction) directly against city GitHub orgs (cityofchicago, CityOfLosAngeles, cityofboston, etc.) for any committed STR mirrors this web search missed.
